blocks.text: 2. Project name
Project title: Lantern Field Papaya and Vegetable Project. Proposal reference: SYNTHETIC-12A-2026-001; document version 1.0, dated 19 October 2026.
3. Project nature
Proposed land use: Agriculture. Project purpose: establish a small irrigated papaya and vegetable farm for the domestic market on 12 acres under a requested 15-year lease.
4. Project introduction

Project description: A fictional individual-operated agricultural enterprise allocating 6 acres to papaya, 4 acres to seasonal vegetables, 1 acre to access/storage/water infrastructure and 1 acre to conservation/drainage. The plan provides 6 full-time positions including the owner-manager. Initial investment: LKR 12,000,000, entirely fictional owner equity. This is a proposed plan, not an operational farm or approved lease.
5. Proposed land location and lease request

Land location: DEVELOPMENT_MOCK_FARM_12A, on SYNTHETIC TEST ACCESS ROAD R-TEST-01. Project Province: DEVELOPMENT_MOCK_PROVINCE_A; District: DEVELOPMENT_MOCK_DISTRICT; Divisional Secretariat Division: DEVELOPMENT_MOCK_DS; Grama Niladhari Division: DEVELOPMENT_MOCK_GN_001. These are synthetic administrative identifiers for the Development scenario, not real jurisdictions.

rows: 12 acres (4.85622770688 hectares). The entire synthetic parcel is requested.

blocks.text: 6. Existing business registration — inapplicability

No existing business is being extended or relocated. This is a proposed new individual enterprise. Existing-business registration details are therefore inapplicable. No registration certificate is claimed or attached. Any registration needed for actual operations would be obtained separately; this declaration is synthetic source evidence for template applicability only.
7. Ownership form

The applicant is an Individual / proposed sole proprietor. Requested tenure is leasehold only; freehold ownership of the land is not claimed. The project is not a company, partnership or cooperative. No actual land allocation, title, consent or official approval is asserted.
8. Initial buildings and structures

Planned initial construction: one simple single-storey, open-sided crop packing/storage shed, 80 square metres, and a 20-square-metre water-tank base. Total structural footprint: 100 square metres, within the 1-acre infrastructure allocation. No residence, factory or worker accommodation is proposed. Estimated shed cost is LKR 900,000; the tank/base and drip network are included in the LKR 2,100,000 irrigation allocation. Required construction and access permissions are not yet granted.

blocks.text: 10. Future buildings over the 15-year period — inapplicability

No additional buildings or expansion of the 100-square-metre initial structural footprint are planned during years 1–15 (2027–2041). The initial 80-square-metre shed and 20-square-metre tank base will be maintained. Future additional-building descriptions/areas are inapplicable because none are planned. Any later proposal to construct more would require a separately reviewed revision and applicable permissions; it is not approved by this document.
11. Future development layout

The 12-acre boundary allocation remains unchanged for all 15 requested years. Years 1–5: establish crops and stabilize irrigation. Years 6–10: renew papaya blocks progressively within the same 6 acres; continue vegetable rotation within 4 acres. Years 11–15: renew equipment, maintain drainage and prepare an end-of-term land-restoration plan. No new building, adjacent parcel or extra acreage is included.

13. Employment plan

Expected employment: 6 full-time positions, including the owner-manager and 5 hired staff. All salary values are fictional planning allowances. No seasonal positions are counted in the six-person total.
14. Raw material and input sources

Raw-material requirements apply to this agricultural project. Planned inputs and sources are fictional procurement assumptions, not supply agreements. Initial planting stock is a separate startup cost; recurring materials below are operating inputs.

blocks.text: 15. Recurring raw-material costs

The LKR 90,000 monthly input subtotal is included once in the monthly operating budget on page 7. The LKR 1,400,000 startup planting allocation on page 8 establishes the farm; it is not included again in recurring inputs.
16. Current domestic market

As a new unestablished project, current sales and signed customer contracts are zero. The assumed target market consists of domestic fresh-produce wholesalers and local retailers in the fictional DEVELOPMENT_MOCK_DISTRICT. The planning price is LKR 100 per kilogram for both papaya and mixed vegetables. This is a synthetic price assumption, not a market quotation, secured price or guaranteed demand.
17. Future marketing and foreign-market inapplicability

Domestic strategy: grade produce at the shed, use reusable crates, schedule two consolidated collections weekly at maturity and seek two independent wholesale buyers after permission to operate. Keep batch and complaint records and adjust crop timing to demand. Foreign-market strategy is inapplicable: no exports, foreign buyers, export revenue or foreign-market certification are proposed during the 15-year test plan. No buyer agreement or certification is claimed.
18. Project turnover projections

All forecasts use constant fictional 2026 LKR prices. The first operating year assumes half of steady-state production while crops establish; years 2 and 3 assume steady production. Turnover is gross sales, not investment, profit or secured revenue.

Demand and price risk: maintain multiple prospective buyers and crop rotation; review actual prices monthly. No public procurement order, guaranteed offtake or official marketing approval is asserted.

pages.title: 07 | Sales estimates and monthly working capital

blocks.text: 19. Sales-income calculation
Steady-state annual sales for 2028 and 2029 reconcile to LKR 14,000,000. The 2027 half-output assumption yields LKR 7,000,000.
20. Monthly working-capital budget

Monthly operating cash requirement: LKR 500,000. Annual operating cash requirement: LKR 6,000,000. Initial six-month working-capital reserve: LKR 3,000,000 (6 × 500,000), included within the LKR 12,000,000 initial investment. The reserve is a financing allocation, not an extra operating expense.

Lease rent and taxes are not known and are excluded from this operating illustration; their amounts must be determined separately. They are not assumed to be zero. No debt is planned, so financing interest is not included. Financial viability would need reassessment once actual rent, taxes and permissions are known.

23A. Cash reconciliation — not additional investment

At establishment, LKR 12,000,000 owner equity funds LKR 9,000,000 capital expenditure and LKR 3,000,000 opening reserve. Subsequent projected sales fund operating costs. No second equity injection or double counting of the reserve is assumed. Price/yield downside and actual lease charges may reduce these surpluses.

Planning date: 19 October 2026. Requested lease duration: 15 years. If not, all start dates must be rebaselined; this programme is not authority to occupy or build.

blocks.text: Management controls: maintain payroll, sales, water, crop-input and maintenance logs. Review output (target 140,000 kg/year at steady state), six-person employment, operating cash cost (LKR 6,000,000/year) and drainage condition quarterly. Correct deviations through a documented revised plan; do not treat this schedule as an institutional approval.
25. Environmental impacts and mitigation

Predicted risks include soil erosion, nutrient runoff, water demand, packaging waste and equipment noise. Mitigation plan: preserve the 1-acre conservation/drainage block; use vegetated margins and contour beds; schedule drip irrigation by soil moisture; compost suitable organic residue; segregate and return containers; prevent chemical discharge; maintain a spill kit; work in daylight. The LKR 15,000 monthly monitoring allowance supports logs and periodic checks. These are proposed measures, not an environmental impact assessment, clearance or evidence of site suitability.
26. Sustainability and maintenance

Rotate vegetables within 4 acres, renew papaya within 6 acres, maintain the 1-acre infrastructure area and retain the 1-acre conservation allocation for all 15 years. Inspect drip lines weekly, drainage monthly and the shed/tank quarterly; budget LKR 20,000/month for repairs. Record water use, soil cover, input use, staff training and waste transfers. Use the domestic marketing plan to spread demand risk. End-of-term intention is orderly restoration under the actual lease terms, not an assumed extension or handoff approval.
